rules.body: Apply when edits use reusable trailing work, document buffers outlive view subscriptions, and synchronous callbacks may navigate. Establish the departure policy separately rather than requiring persistence-before-return as an applicability premise. README.md states: "A workspace document buffer persists independently of the current view badge. Save callbacks can synchronously navigate."

Bind deferred text to its originating document, replace the pending value on each edit, and restart the quiet interval. Preserve valid empty text and later bursts. TASK states: "Coalesce edits using the existing trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet\ninterval, write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts\nmust continue to save." In src/workflow.go, the document-bound task is created with "NewTrailing(env,120,func(text string){env.Write(id,text)})".

Consume the completed batch before invoking callback-capable saving, so a synchronous callback can enqueue later work without the outer flush erasing it or saving the consumed batch twice. Preserve src/workflow.go's ordering: "text:=t.pending;t.handle=nil;t.pending=nil\n    if text!=nil { t.work(*text) }".

Keep document responsibility separate from removal of the current view subscription. Do not cancel or discard document work merely because its badge detaches; preserve document binding and same-document reuse. docs/host-api.md states: "Document buffers are owned by a separate BufferBank service, while Badge owns only a live subscription." Require flushing before departure returns only when the original task or public behavioral documentation establishes that policy.

Preserve authority of newer navigation across synchronous callbacks. Publish retirement state before callback-capable cleanup or saving, finish cleanup of captured old resources, and prevent an older Open from installing its destination after reentrant navigation. docs/host-api.md states: "A store listener may call navigation synchronously." src/workflow.go captures "request:=w.generation" before retirement and checks "if true&&request!=w.generation{return}" afterward. If adding departure saving, include it inside the region protected by that ownership check.

Preserve public interfaces, document identity and text, the no-current-view edit guard, document-specific status filtering, and payload semantics. docs/host-api.md states: "All source identities/text and status payloads retain original semantics." Keep preview work independent: TASK states: "Preserve the editor's other behavior and public interfaces.\nThe adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change." src/workflow.go retains "NewTrailing(env,40" for preview and "func(p *Preview)Hide(){p.task.Cancel()}".

Use controlled timers and synchronous callbacks to check deadline restart, no early write within an uninterrupted burst, latest text including empty text, subsequent bursts, original-document binding, pending work after switch/close/dispose, same-document reopening, status subscription cleanup, and nested navigation during saving. Check preview's 40 ms delay, hide cancellation and later reuse. Evaluate departure completion timing only against an independently established departure policy; keep evaluation expectations separate from source-supported obligations.

limitations: The task and non-evaluation public documents do not establish that pending text must be saved before departure returns. Persistence independent of the badge does not alone choose between flushing on departure and retaining scheduled work.

Attempts 1 and 2 provide implementation observations, not additional requirements. Attempt 2 passing does not prove that departure flushing is required, causally sufficient, or beneficial across tasks.
The supplied Environment interface does not establish additional failure, timer cancellation, or scheduling behavior.
This revision refines applicability and checkpoints; it does not disprove the predecessor's conditional guidance for systems with an explicit persistence-before-return requirement.

notes: Not approved; training acceptance or expert summary does not verify cross-task effectiveness
